endpoints.screen: Appointment Detail → Charge customer (owner / front desk)
endpoints.description: The final charge at checkout (PaymentKind.CHARGE on the server), for an in_progress booking. The amount is the balance: totalAmount minus any deposit already paid. Same shape as start-booking-payment so both use one polling pattern. method 'cash': records it immediately and returns 200 with the Booking (status completed, paymentStatus paid, paymentMethod cash). method 'mpesa': sends an STK push to phone (any Kenyan format; defaults to the booking's customerPhone) routed to the business's own till/paybill/bank, and returns 202 at once. The app then polls GET /bookings/{bookingId} every 3s for up to ~2 min: success = status completed + paymentStatus paid, with paymentReference (M-Pesa receipt) and paymentMethod mpesa set; failure = chargePayment.status failed | timeout with a failureReason (same values as depositPayment). The customer can be re-prompted after a failure. No balance due (deposit covered everything): mpesa behaves like cash and completes immediately. If an M-Pesa charge lands after the booking was already paid another way (e.g. cash while the prompt was open), it's recorded as a refund owed (refund.status due). App: AppointmentDetailScreen's Charge customer sheet (src/api/booking.ts#chargeBookingPayment polls until paid or failed).

endpoints.description: Revenue trend buckets, payment-method breakdown, per-service breakdown, per-transaction ledger, and appointment counts for a date range (`from`/`to` query params, both 'YYYY-MM-DD'). Also takes an optional `staffId` query param — when present, scopes every number to bookings assigned to that team member (see create-walk-in-booking's staffId), which is what TeamMemberDetailScreen's earnings section needs; omitted, it's the whole-business view EarningsScreen shows. Mirrors what src/utils/earnings.ts currently computes client-side by filtering every booking in memory — fine for mock data, not something a real backend should do at scale. `services` should include every service the business currently offers, not just ones with revenue (bookingsCount: 0 rows included) — both screens use that to show what isn't selling, not just what is. `transactions` is one row per service actually performed (not per booking), newest first — the client caps this at 10 for preset ranges and shows everything for a custom range, so a real backend could paginate rather than always returning every row, but the mock returns the full set and lets the client slice it. Only bookings with paymentStatus 'paid' count toward any amount here.

endpoints.auth: the business owner, or its front desk
endpoints.description: Assigns an unassigned booking, or reassigns an assigned one. The staff member must offer every service on the booking, work that weekday, and be free (including room for the business's other unassigned bookings at that time). Only pending_payment, confirmed and in_progress bookings can be (re)assigned. App: AppointmentDetailScreen's Assign staff / Reassign sheet, which stays open on staff_unavailable. Unassigned bookings are found with list-business-bookings?unassigned=true (Manage Business → Unassigned bookings).

endpoints.description: earned = commission on paid bookings; available = earned − pending − paid.
